must_contain: Additional copies are available from:
Office of Communication, Outreach, and Development
This guidance represents the current thinking of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) on this topic.
This guidance provides recommendations to industry on formal meetings between the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and sponsors or applicants
This guidance has been prepared by the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research in cooperation with the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research at the Food and Drug Administration.
This guidance finalizes the draft guidance of the same name issued in August 2023.
As part of the reauthorization of the Biosimilar User Fee Act (BsUFA), the FDA has committed to specific performance goals
There are six types of formal meetings that occur between requesters and FDA staff
A BIA meeting is an initial assessment limited to a general discussion regarding whether licensure under section 351(k) of the PHS Act may be feasible for a particular product
Any guidance already received from other health authorities on product development.
Requesting a BIA meeting is not a requirement prior to joining the BPD program.
A BPD Type 1 meeting is a meeting that is necessary for an otherwise stalled development program to proceed or a meeting to address an important safety issue.
Meetings to discuss an important safety issue, when such an issue is identified and the FDA and requester agree that the issue should be discussed.
Immunogenicity testing strategy following prior FDA recommendations or feedback.
This meeting type includes substantive review of full study reports
Full study report(s) for a clinical study or studies.
Proposal for justification of extrapolation
Discussion of any potential review issues identified based on the information provided
No fee is associated with a BIA meeting.
Requesters may request this meeting format only for BIA, BPD Type 2a, and BPD Type 2b meetings.
To promote efficient meeting management, requesters should anticipate future needs
The FDA considers meeting requests sent by fax or email to be courtesy copies only and are not substitutes for formal submissions.
Proper and proprietary names of the reference product.
Human factors engineering plan (if applicable).
List of specific objectives or outcomes the requester expects from the meeting.
Proposed agenda, including estimated times needed for discussion of each agenda item.
Therefore, a meeting request should include no more than 10 questions listed consecutively regardless of discipline
The FDA honors requests for BPD Type 2b, BPD Type 3, and BPD Type 4 meetings except in the most unusual circumstances.

If a biosimilar biological product development fee is required under section 744H, and the sponsor does not pay the fee within the timeframe required under section 744H, the meeting will be cancelled.
Denials are based on substantive reason, not merely on the absence of a minor element of the meeting request or a minor element of the meeting package.
If the requested date for any meeting type is greater than the specified time frame, the meeting date should be within 14 calendar days of the requested date.

notes: FDA guidance PDF (23 pages as served, tagged), cut to pages 1-15 with pypdf (see holdout2/SELECTION.md): page 1 cover, page 2 inner cover with contact addresses, page 3 table of contents, pages 4-15 = guidance pages 1-12 (sections I-VII; section VIII starts on the next page, which is not in the file). Headings: the title (its first printed line 'Formal Meetings' on the covers; on page 4 the title is three bold centred lines starting 'Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors'), 'TABLE OF CONTENTS', the seven Roman-numbered bold section headings and the eight lettered bold subsection headings in sections III and VII, each listed without its number or letter so that either form matches; 'MEETING TYPES' carries a superscript footnote mark 7 in print. 'MEETING REQUESTS' (VI.) also occurs inside the VII. heading; the one-to-one heading match keeps them apart. The table-of-contents entries repeat the headings but are not headings. The bold lead-ins of the numbered list in section V ('Face-to-Face:', 'In-person:', 'Teleconference:') are list text, not headings. Table captions ('Table 1:' ...) are captions. Tables: the three page-15 tables are complete; each header cell is printed on two or three centred lines and is written joined with spaces. Footnotes: 2 of the 33 must_contain phrases are footnotes (1 and 18); 2 are list items with dash markers (section III.E), 4 are numbered list items. Many sentences in the file contain curly quotes or typographic apostrophes ('FDA’s', '“core”'); no phrase or anchor contains a quote, apostrophe, dash or footnote mark. ordered: 8 body-text anchors on guidance pages 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10 and 11 (PDF pages 4-14). Noise: the running header 'Contains Nonbinding Recommendations' is printed at the top of pages 3-15 (13 times), max 1; page numbers are too short to count. The two covers repeat the title and the HHS/FDA/CDER/CBER block by design; that is document text, not page furniture, and is not counted. The text is ragged-right; its only line-end hyphens are in compounds ('non-/core', 'non-/U.S.-licensed') or URLs, so absent is empty. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 90-230 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, mastheads, cover art, chart labels) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
